record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How should photon and dilepton production be computed during the late-stage transition from hydrodynamics to free-streaming hadrons in heavy-ion collision simulations, and when should a macroscopic hydrodynamic emission-rate treatment be replaced or supplemented by a microscopic hadronic-transport calculation that unifies electromagnetic probes with the transport description already used for hadrons?

evidence.quote: The transition from hydrodynamics to hadronic transport in simulations of heavy-ion collisions can also be understood in terms of the relaxation time τ_relax and the evolution time τ_evolution discussed earlier.
This effectively leads to the inverse processes listed in Table 1: hydrodynamics transitioning towards free-streaming.
Computing photons and dileptons production in the transition from hydrodynamics to free-streaming hadrons is challenging.

It is still common to use a macroscopic approach (Eqs 1 and 2) to perform this calculation: the hydrodynamic simulation is continued to later times, and combined with a photon or a dilepton emission rate.
However, important work has been done to compute electromagnetic emission microscopically instead, using hadronic transport

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In a numerical simulation of a relativistic heavy-ion collision, the hot QCD matter is modeled in successive stages. In an intermediate stage the medium is described by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics, characterized at each spacetime point by local temperature T(x), flow velocity u^μ(x), and dissipative corrections (shear stress, bulk pressure, baryon diffusion). In this stage, the spectrum of electromagnetic probes (real photons and dileptons of invariant mass M) is obtained from a macroscopic formula of the schematic form

  E dN_γ/d^3p = ∫ d^4x  Γ_γ(E·u(x), T(x); δf)  ,
  d^4N_ℓℓ / d^4q  = ∫ d^4x  Γ_ℓℓ(q·u(x), M, T(x); δf)  ,

where Γ_γ and Γ_ℓℓ are thermal emission rates (per unit four-volume) computed from the in-medium electromagnetic spectral function and δf denotes off-equilibrium corrections. In a later stage, once the medium becomes sufficiently dilute, the dynamics is described by a microscopic hadronic transport (Boltzmann-type) cascade evolving discrete hadrons through binary scatterings and resonance decays; in this stage electromagnetic emission can be obtained microscopically by summing 2→2+γ, 2→2+ℓℓ, and resonance decay contributions along the simulated hadronic trajectories.

Let τ_relax(x) denote the local microscopic relaxation time of the hadronic medium and τ_evolution(x) the local macroscopic expansion time scale (e.g. 1/(∂·u)). Address the following:

(a) Formulate a quantitatively justified prescription, valid throughout the transition region where τ_relax(x) and τ_evolution(x) become comparable, for computing the photon spectrum E dN_γ/d^3p and the dilepton spectrum d^4N_ℓℓ/d^4q so that the result smoothly interpolates between the hydrodynamic emission-rate formula above and the microscopic transport-based emission, avoiding both double counting and omission.

(b) Identify a criterion (in terms of T(x), τ_relax(x)/τ_evolution(x), or other locally computable quantities) that determines, at each spacetime point, whether the macroscopic hydrodynamic emission-rate treatment should be replaced or supplemented by the microscopic hadronic-transport calculation, and demonstrate that the resulting unified description for electromagnetic probes is consistent with the transport description already used for the hadronic sector (i.e. the same particle content, cross sections, and off-equilibrium distributions).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews on electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions (2023–2025) continue to flag the late-stage transition between hydrodynamic emission and hadronic-transport emission as an unresolved modeling issue, with most state-of-the-art codes still relying on macroscopic emission-rate formulas extended into the dilute regime. No unified, transport-consistent prescription has been established.

status_evidence.title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Computing photons and dileptons production in the transition from hydrodynamics to free-streaming hadrons is challenging.
status_evidence.claim: The transition between hydrodynamic and transport descriptions for EM probes is identified as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: SMASH-vHLLE-hybrid and dilepton/photon emission studies
status_evidence.snippet: Recent hybrid simulations continue to treat photon and dilepton emission via thermal rates folded with hydro evolution, with hadronic-transport contributions added separately.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, no unified microscopic-macroscopic prescription exists; the issue remains open.
